I've been working on developing an idea I've had for some time now, using the TOR onion routing network to build a social network similar to Twitter/GAB etc. The design I've been working on (mostly in planning, but I have created some proof-of-concept code to make sure it actually works in practice) centers around these features.

  • Truly peer-to-peer. Absolutely no server infrastructure required, beside distributing the software itself. I use TORs hidden service features to provide identity and let nodes exchange data directly. You pull posts from your subscriptions directly using their hidden service ID.
  • Anonymity as guaranteed by the TOR network. A discussion can be had as to wether or not that is good enough, as there has been speculations about compromised nodes, particularly exit nodes. Traffic will never leave the TOR network however so I think it should be "good enough".
  • Message authentication via cryptographic signatures. The TOR hidden service system is based on public/private keys, and these will be used to sign messages. That means that even though you are anonymous, your unique ID (or hidden service descriptor) can be used to verify a cryptographic signature. This lets us verify that messages originated from whom they say they did, and that they have not been altered in any way.
  • Censorship resistant. While I would add features for individuals to be able to block/ignore speciffic accounts, outright censoring or banning anyone would be technically impossible since there is no central server. Yes that means illegal content would be very much possible (and knowing the internet, probably likely).

Of course, this approach comes with some drawbacks, some of which may be fatal. This is why I am posting this here, because I need input. If you have a solution to any of these, or you know any I may have missed, please to let me know.

  • A thick client would be required; that is, this will for obvious reasons not be a web service
  • The client would need to be online in order to communicate with the network, meaning ideally 24/7
  • Scalability is my biggest concern. Twitter can "scale" by throwing more servers online; but here the users themselves would be "hosting" the content. That means that if you are Donald Trump you would need to run it on a pretty beefy 24/7 online machine with a good internet connection...

There are other more techincal challenges but those can be dealt with as far as I can see. Does this look like a viable project to you? Any other concerns? Do you have any programming experience and/or intimate knowledge of the TOR network and some spare time to contribute?

I have not set a platform in stone yet, but the proof-of-concept code I have developed is based on Python and the STEM library. Also looking into Twisted and various message queueing frameworks. I chose this because I am currently trying to develop my Python skills and it seems to have the most mature supporting libraries (i.e. less coding).

On the off chance you are wondering who the hell I am, I am posting this from an alt account as I am not yet sure where this project is heading. I would not like to have it associated with my main account (which can be trivially linked to my real life identity). Guess I'm weird like that.
